Eslamdoust et al. (2026) DBH–height models for Ontario tree species

Source: R/hd_eslamdoust2026.R
hd_eslamdoust2026.Rd

Vectorized implementation of the population-level individual-tree height–diameter models M4 and M5 of Eslamdoust et al. (2026) for eight tree species of the boreal and mixed (Great Lakes–St. Lawrence) forests of Ontario. Predicts total tree height (m) from DBH (cm) alone (M4) or from DBH and three stand-level predictors: dominant stand height, basal area and stand density (M5).

Usage

hd_eslamdoust2026(
  DBH,
  species,
  HDOM = NULL,
  BA = NULL,
  TPH = NULL,
  keep_model_id = FALSE
)

Arguments

DBH

Numeric vector. Tree level. Diameter at breast height (1.3 m above ground), in cm. Must be >= 0.

species

Character vector. Tree level. NFI species codes (e.g. "ACER.SAH"; compact "ACERSAH" is accepted).

HDOM

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Stand height (m): "mean height of dominant and co-dominant trees" in the plot (source "SHT", p. 219). The source does not state whether all species or only the subject species are included. Must be > 0. Supply with BA and TPH to use M5.

BA

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Stand basal area (m²/ha) (source "BAH", p. 219 and p. 220). The source does not state a minimum DBH or species basis for this total. Must be > 0.

TPH

Optional numeric vector. Plot level. Number of trees per hectare "with DBH\(\ge\) 2.5cm" (source "TPH", p. 220). Must be > 0.

keep_model_id

Logical. If TRUE, add column model_id ("eslamdoust2026_m4" or "eslamdoust2026_m5").

Value

A tibble with column height (m) and, if keep_model_id = TRUE, model_id.

Details

Model scope (species coverage): eastern white pine (PINU.STR), eastern white cedar (THUJ.OCC), sugar maple (ACER.SAH), yellow birch (BETU.ALL), American beech (FAGU.GRA), tamarack (LARI.LAR), basswood (TILI.AME) and eastern hemlock (TSUG.CAN). Fitted to Ontario growth-and-yield and NFI plots in natural stands (Table 1, p. 219), with stand basal area \(\ge\) 5 m²/ha.

Model forms (eqs. 4 and 5, p. 220): $$M4: H = 1.3 + \alpha_0 [1 - \exp(-\alpha_1 DBH)]^{\alpha_2};$$ $$M5: H = 1.3 + \alpha_0 \, HDOM^{\alpha_1} [1 - \exp(-\alpha_2 (TPH / BA)^{\alpha_3} DBH)]^{\alpha_4}.$$

Height convention: total tree height; DBH measured at 1.3 m, so predicted height tends to 1.3 m as DBH tends to 0.

Population-level prediction: coefficients are the fixed effects of the mixed-effects fits (Tables 4 and 5, p. 225), evaluated with the plot-level random effect on \(\alpha_0\) set to zero (\(u = 0\)), as in the "fixed response" curves of Fig. 3. Plot-specific calibration with measured heights is not implemented.

Variants: if HDOM, BA and TPH are all NULL (default), M4 (DBH only) is used. If all three are supplied, M5 is used for every species. Supplying only some of them is an error. A one-time message reports the variant used. The authors note that M4 performed as well as or better than M5 for yellow birch and eastern hemlock (and basswood) and that M4 "may be considered a more parsimonious and operationally practical model in cases where stand-level variables are unavailable or unreliable" (p. 222, p. 225).

Tamarack and basswood (M5): the stand-density exponent \(\alpha_3\) is reported as 0 (not significant; Table 5), so BA and TPH do not change their predicted heights; they are still required for M5.

Corrected coefficient: the tamarack M5 \(\alpha_2\) is printed as 0.9793 in Table 5, which gives a near-flat curve (about 16 m at DBH 2.5 cm) inconsistent with Fig. 3b and the fitting data (Table 1). It is treated as a misprint and 0.09793 is used, which reproduces the tamarack curve in Fig. 3b. This value is inferred, not published.

The authors report increased bias for DBH > 50 cm, particularly for white pine, sugar maple, beech and hemlock (p. 225).

Rows with NA in any input return NA height. Inputs outside the per-species range of the fitting data (Table 1: DBH and, for M5, HDOM, BA and TPH) are computed and reported in a single warning.

References

Eslamdoust, J., Vasiliauskas, S., Little, T., and Ashiq, M. W. (2026). Height–diameter modeling of tree species in boreal and mixed forests using a mixed-effects approach and stand-level variables. Forest Science and Technology, 22(1), 217–230. doi:10.1080/21580103.2025.2571222

See also

hd_model_registry(), get_hd_model_info()

Examples

# M4: DBH only
hd_eslamdoust2026(DBH = c(10, 25, 40), species = c("ACER.SAH", "PINU.STR", "TSUG.CAN"))
#> hd_eslamdoust2026(): `HDOM`, `BA` and `TPH` not supplied; using model M4 (DBH
#> only).
#> This message is displayed once per session.
#> # A tibble: 3 × 1
#>   height
#>    <dbl>
#> 1   12.8
#> 2   19.2
#> 3   20.6

# M5: with dominant height, basal area and stems/ha
hd_eslamdoust2026(
  DBH = c(10, 25, 40),
  species = c("ACER.SAH", "PINU.STR", "TSUG.CAN"),
  HDOM = 22, BA = 30, TPH = 1200,
  keep_model_id = TRUE
)
#> hd_eslamdoust2026(): `HDOM`, `BA` and `TPH` supplied; using model M5 (DBH and
#> stand variables).
#> This message is displayed once per session.
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   height model_id         
#>    <dbl> <chr>            
#> 1   13.7 eslamdoust2026_m5
#> 2   19.6 eslamdoust2026_m5
#> 3   20.8 eslamdoust2026_m5

# Inside dplyr::mutate() with tree and plot data
trees <- data.frame(
  DBH = c(12, 25, 18),
  species = c("FAGU.GRA", "BETU.ALL", "THUJ.OCC"),
  HDOM = c(20, 20, 15), BA = c(28, 28, 40), TPH = c(1500, 1500, 3000)
)
dplyr::mutate(trees, hd_eslamdoust2026(DBH, species, HDOM, BA, TPH))
#>   DBH  species HDOM BA  TPH    height
#> 1  12 FAGU.GRA   20 28 1500 13.300521
#> 2  25 BETU.ALL   20 28 1500 20.650416
#> 3  18 THUJ.OCC   15 40 3000  9.243844
